opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Requires BES membership. Not available to cover principal researcher salary, bench fees; not a scholarship; cannot fund projects forming part of a funded fellowship. Requires two reference statements.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard that advances ecological science.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; not required for all group members. Groups of 8-15 diverse interdisciplinary members across career stages, institutions and with international participation; must demonstrate EDI principles.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracks innovative and impactful research by funding the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 individuals to focus on data analysis and synthesis.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: £3,500 for first five years (approx £500/year), with an additional £3,500 claimable in year 6

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers, consultants and university academics. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with at least 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies such as restoration, habitat creation, alien species control and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level, no geographical restrictions. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Projects max 12 months. Funding unavailable for work forming part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices in ecology, providing evidence-based examples of innovative practice, systematic reviews, exploring emerging education research areas, and disseminating best practices in teaching and learning.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations. Undergraduates and masters students not eligible. Requires employer/supervisor approval and a willing host organisation. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding placements of up to 12 months in a distinctly different discipline or sector, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels. Projects max 12 months, no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work. Proposals must target a non-academic audience.
opportunities.summary: Supports BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: max £500 for in-person events; max £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (not postdocs, undergraduates or masters students). Must work/study at a university or research institution and work in the science of ecology. Must give a presentation if attending a meeting. Must be at least three years since a previous BES training and travel grant.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to present their work at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system. Round 3 opens 24 August 2026.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage, be a citizen of and based in a Global South country, travel from and return to that country, have applied to present at the Annual Meeting, and be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending the meeting such as registration, transport, food and accommodation. Open 17 July - 8 September 2026, selected by lottery.
